liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hey Pockey Way** (1 review): The reviewer liked hearing Hey Pockey Way, a tune they had never heard before [40]
- **I Will Take You Home/** (1 review): The source singles out the transition from I Will Take You Home to Drums as top notch [38]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.morris.crazyfingers.106587.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 145 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: The FOB recording is sonically perfect, easily mistaken for a soundboard but distinct [36]
- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.carpenter.andrewf.92586.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 149 min [2]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.92585.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.98647.dvda**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 0 min [8]
- **gd1988-07-03.nakcm304.beyerm101.suraci.82801.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [25]. Said about its sound: Audience noises capture anticipation and rapt attention, reflecting the crowd's blissful moments [32]

## Around the show

- A hand glider flew into the stadium, making the band nervous and ending the set early [31]
- The venue was quiet, serene, and wooded, creating a peaceful and beautiful atmosphere [33]
- Weather was terrific, with a lively parking lot circus and brisk vendor trade [34]
- The second show on the 4th was marked by snow, surprising for summer in Maine [37]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.morris.crazyfingers.106587.flac16**: taped by Bob Morris; transferred by Chuck T.; source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM-300 (CP-4) x2 > Cassette Master (Sony TCD5M/TDK MA 90) [1]. Also: The setlist includes a sequence from Hell In A Bucket through Not Fade Away [1]
- **gd1988-07-03.nak300.carpenter.andrewf.92586.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Nakamichi CM-300's w/CP-4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's with no Dolby [2]. Also: A patch from ShnID-82801 covers a tape flip during I Will Take You Home [2]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.92585.flac16**: transferred by Dan Haugh; source: SBD (3908) + AUD (82801) + AUD (3325) [3]. Also: The show is seamless, with a break after I Will Take You Home before Drums [3]
- **gd1988-07-03.mtx.haugh.98647.dvda**: taped by See Info file; transferred by Surround sound by Dan Haugh; source: DVD-Audio 5.1 Surround Sound (MLP Encoded 6ch x 16/44) [8]. Also: SBD source used Nakamichi CM304s and Beyer M101s, transferred by Tony Suraci [8]
- **gd1988-07-03.nakcm304.beyerm101.suraci.82801.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nak CM304's+Beyer M101>Sony Mixer>Sony D5M [25]

claims.text: A hand glider flew into the stadium, making the band nervous and ending the set early
Audience noises capture anticipation and rapt attention, reflecting the crowd's blissful moments
The venue was quiet, serene, and wooded, creating a peaceful and beautiful atmosphere
Weather was terrific, with a lively parking lot circus and brisk vendor trade
The FOB recording is sonically perfect, easily mistaken for a soundboard but distinct
The second show on the 4th was marked by snow, surprising for summer in Maine
The source singles out the transition from I Will Take You Home to Drums as top notch
The reviewer liked hearing Hey Pockey Way, a tune they had never heard before
The setlist includes a sequence from Hell In A Bucket through Not Fade Away
A patch from ShnID-82801 covers a tape flip during I Will Take You Home
The show is seamless, with a break after I Will Take You Home before Drums
SBD source used Nakamichi CM304s and Beyer M101s, transferred by Tony Suraci
